key_insight: A physics-informed neural network with exact boundary and initial constraints recovers the shear piezoelectric coefficient e15 accurately from sparse, noisy simulated wavefields.
engineering_relevance: The approach could enable non-destructive characterization of shear-mode coupling for PMUT and surface acoustic wave devices without dedicated resonance-test specimens.
method: Embed spatial distance functions and temporal multipliers in network outputs to enforce boundary and initial conditions exactly.
Train on coupled electro-elastodynamic equations and sparse observations, without boundary or initial-condition penalty weights.
Non-dimensionalize the governing equations to improve coefficient scaling.
evidence_signal: On finite-element data sampled along one subsurface line, the full formulation achieved 1.19% mean e15 error at 30 dB noise and 0.65–2.71% across a 40–0 dB noise sweep.
watch_item: Validation is simulation-only; robustness to experimental measurements, uncertain boundary conditions, and material-model mismatch remains untested.
paper_title: Identifying the Shear Piezoelectric Coefficient using Physics-Informed Neural Networks under Exact Boundary and Initial Constraints
